Lopuszno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Łopuszno, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Łopuszno developed from the 18th century, supported by the village's owners, Franciszek and Eustachy Dobiecki; the community reached 750 people by 1928, and Jews made up 74 percent of the local population the year before WWII began. In 1940, Jews from nearby villages were resettled into Łopuszno, and in September 1942, all Jews from the ghetto were deported via Chęciny to Treblinka. This cemetery, most likely established in the 18th century, was destroyed by the Germans during WWII, its tombstones used to pave the front of the local gendarmerie station; executions were also carried out at the site.
